confirmed_with_recorded_caveat.note: Quotes verbatim at Robbins Schug et al. 2012, p. 138. Caveat recorded in the cell's note: the article's 'mature' attaches at period level to the Period III urban horizon (Cemetery R-37 and IIIB); the article uses 'the mature period' as its site-level name for that horizon (pp. 138, 144, 145).

method: Independent second pass: a separate agent opened every cited locator for every MAPPED cell (24 cells as built, 28 in the draft) and read the determination there, with named attacks on the four judgment calls. No cell was edited into agreement; challenges were reclassified under the rules and are recorded below and in the affected cells' adjudication notes in determinations.json.

reclassifications.from: MAPPED / MATURE (draft, by scheme inheritance from Robbins Schug et al. 2012, p. 138)
reclassifications.reason: The second pass searched every occurrence of 'mature' in the article: all attach to Cemetery R-37 / Period IIIB specifically; no sentence assigns Period III as a whole, or IIIA/IIIC, to the mature period. The inheritance was an analyst's extension (date-span equation plus subdivisions imported from Kenoyer & Meadow 2010), not the publication's own assignment of the scheme. No second admissible reading assigns these cells a coarse period; the era-framework assignments reported by locator aids (Phase-139 register citing Kenoyer 2008; Schuldenrein et al. 2007, Table 1) are not verified to the section 3.3 bar. Per section 7.4 the cells are reclassified, not edited into agreement.

reprobes.outcome: NOT READ in the journal itself. strengthenings.note: Second pass located a more explicit locator in the same publication: Bisht 2015, sealings chapter, p. 308 - 'mature Harappan phase, i.e. Stages IV and V'. The determination record now cites it alongside the chronology table (p. 104), whose affinity reading the pass also confirmed.

Second pass confirmed Period IV inside the Indus span in Jarrige, Didier & Quivron 2011's own framing (p. 9: the Indus civilization's three main periods, the Nausharo sequence II-III-IV consistent with it; p. 30: Nausharo IV contemporary with Harappa 3C) and quoted the fuller p. 9 passage, now carried in the cell's evidence quote.
